Misc. File No. 4247Y
Dixwell Road Station,
No. 2971
REPORT
Date June 22. 19 37
Subject Private Investigation Bureau at 20 Lincoln Terrace.
Made by D.S.I. Cumming Forwarded by Jrmalson Inspector

Sir,
With reference to the attached advertisement in the Personal Column of the 'China Press' of June 17th, 1937, advertising a private investigation bureau at 20 Lincoln Terrace, O.O.L., I have to report that D.S.I. Chu Tsi Huang (Hangkew), representing himself as a prospective client, visited the address in question at 3 p.m. 21-6-37. He was received at the door by a servant who asked him to wait. The servant then re-entered the house and on his return shortly afterwards, stated that his master was out. He, however, asked the detective to leave his name, address and business, saying that his master would call on him afterwards. The detective left a note giving his name and address (Lane 61/8 Medhurst Road) and saying that he solicited their help in collecting certain accounts.

At 8.20 p.m. on the same evening two foreigners called at the detective's home. One of them presented a business card bearing the following particulars :- "F.G. Horst, Chief Operator, The World Protection and Investigation Bureau, 20 Lincoln Terrace, off Kiang-wen Road." He gave his nationality as German and stated that he had been in the same line of business in China for the last 17 years and was in touch with all important business concerns in Shanghai. He specialized in credit information, accounts collecting and shadowing and obtaining evidence in matrimonial cases. His companion gave his name as George Nielsen, American Citizen, born in Denmark. They stated that their terms for accounts collecting were $10.00 down payment and 10% of all sums collected.

During his conversation with the men, the detective formed the opinion that they were probably endeavouring to promote an honest business. There is no record under these names at the

报告
日期：1937 年 6 月 22 日
事由：林肯台 20 号的私人调查局。
呈报人：副巡官卡明（D.S.I. Cumming） 转呈人：督察贾马尔森（Jrmalson）

敬启者：
关于附上的 1937 年 6 月 17 日《字林西报》（China Press）个人专栏中刊登的广告，该广告宣传位于林肯台 20 号（O.O.L.）的一家私人调查局，本人谨此报告，副巡官朱子煌（Chu Tsi Huang，虹口），自称是潜在客户，于 1937 年 6 月 21 日下午 3 时造访了上述地址。一名仆人在门口接待了他，并请他等候。随后该仆人返回屋内，不久后出来说主人不在家。然而，他要求这名侦探留下姓名、地址和来意，称主人稍后会去拜访他。该侦探留下了一张便条，写明其姓名和地址（麦赫斯特路 61/8 弄），并表示希望对方协助催收某些账目。

同日晚上 8 时 20 分，两名外国人来到该侦探家中。其中一人递上一张名片，上面印有以下信息：“F.G. Horst，首席办事员，世界保护与调查局，江湾路旁林肯台 20 号。”他自称国籍为德国，并声称过去 17 年间一直在中国从事同一行业，与上海所有重要的商业机构都有联系。他专门从事信用信息、账款催收、跟踪以及在婚姻案件中获取证据。他的同伴自称乔治·尼尔森（George Nielsen），美国公民，出生于丹麦。他们声称，其账款催收的收费标准是预付定金 10.00 美元，外加所收款项的 10%。

在与这两人交谈期间，该侦探认为他们可能正试图开展一项正当业务。在这些名字下没有记录
